Czechoslovakia
Czechoslovakia is a country in Central Europe that borders Poland and Germany to the north, Austria and Hungary to the south, Romania to the east, and Germany to the west. The Republic of Czechoslovakia was officially formed in 1918 after the end of the First World War. The center of the Czechoslovak government is Prague, which is considered one of the oldest and most beautiful cities in the world. This country is of great importance in its geography and political structure. The people of Czechoslovakia are two major ethnic groups called Czechs and Slovaks, who have historically lived together. This country is also very advanced in terms of industry and culture and has a special position in Central European politics.

Regarding the issue of Pashtun land in the context of the Indian government's sale of surplus land, much has been considered by the Indian government concerning discrimination and bias between Hindus and Muslims regarding land. However, this question arises in the context of solving the Pashtun land problem in India, specifically regarding the government's sale of Pashtun lands at a time when the Indian government is paying attention to people in all regions engaged in agriculture. For a long time, it has attempted to provide financial and agricultural equipment support to improve agriculture. While many Pashtuns are in the process of selling their agricultural lands, the government has taken certain measures to resolve their problems, including imposing restrictions on the sale of Pashtun lands, providing assistance to increase agricultural production, and offering facilities in land allocation. According to some Pashtuns, as part of the government's policy on land distribution, and while the Indian government is taking steps to resolve their issues, there are still challenges in land allocation and the implementation of agricultural development projects. Despite the measures taken by the government to improve land development and agricultural affairs, some problems remain, necessitating the implementation of a comprehensive government policy to help resolve the issue of Pashtun lands.

In reality, the Turkish government, which was formed in Ankara under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Pasha as a result of the national uprising after the fall of the Ottoman Empire, was going through a difficult period. After the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Turkey was facing the threat of occupation at the hands of its enemies. But the Turkish nation, through this national uprising, was able to gain independence and stand firmly against the invaders.
1229.left: At this stage, as an important decision by Turkey's national leaders, the issue of paying off the Ottoman Empire's debts arose. The new Turkish government, in order to protect national independence while settling these debts, began serious negotiations regarding the manner of their repayment, so as to guarantee the country's national wealth and future.

1234.right:
Pashtun Heroism -23- April 1920
Since one considers their own self (nafs) an enemy, because it is always following its own desires against the commands of God (SWT), this very self is the origin of a human's happiness or misery. If a human gains control over their self and guides it in the light of their intellect and Sharia, then in reality, they become the owner of great successes; and if they drown in the desires of their self, then they become the owner of humiliation and misery in this world and the hereafter. This martyr of ours is also a great example of the sacrifice of these self-desires in the path of God (SWT), and the fact that he reached the status of martyrdom on the battlefield was the result of his good and great deeds, through which he became the owner of eternal life and honor in this world and the hereafter.
Ah! This path of self-sacrifice that this martyr found is a clear sign of his faith and piety. He stood in the field against the enemy with such courage that he cared neither for his head nor for his life; rather, in his heart, he had only the thought of God's (SWT) pleasure and the exaltation of His religion. This spirit of martyrdom of his brought eternal pride and happiness to his family, and his name was written in golden lines on the pages of history.
This martyr, who gave his life for the protection of his homeland and religion, is in reality an example for every Pashtun, who should take a lesson from his bravery and steadfastness in their own deeds and fight against their own self with such determination and courage.
1234.left:
In the paths of the martyrs that we see in our daily lives today, this path of the martyrs' sacrifices is a very great lesson. If we want to be successful in every part of our lives, we must follow in the footsteps of the martyrs and sacrifice our own desires for the pleasure of God (SWT). In this lies the good of every human being in this world and the hereafter, and in this very path lies the way of honor and elevation for every Pashtun.
This blood of the martyrs, which has been shed in the path of truth, is an example of a new light and a new hope that will keep the path of truth bright for future generations as well. We must understand that martyrdom is not just giving one's life, but the name of a sacrifice of a life in which all the desires of one's self are sacrificed for the pleasure of God (SWT).

A summary of a report taken from an issue of the year 1309.

Number fifty

Last week, when a meeting was organized by a number of scholars from the time of Ghazi Amanullah Khan for the awakening of the people of Pashtunkhwa, a decision was made for a great struggle for the freedom of Pashtunkhwa. Many leaders and brave youths from the regions of Pashtunkhwa participated in this meeting. The meeting was chaired by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, who began his speech during the meeting by stating that the awakening of the Pashtun nation is our primary duty. He said that we must break the chains of foreign slavery and unite for independence.

At the end of the meeting, the policy of Ghazi Amanullah Khan was praised, and it was decided that people from every region of Pashtunkhwa would gather for freedom and work to achieve their goal through a joint organization. It was also decided to form a committee under the leadership of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, which would control all the affairs of this movement.
1241.left:
Along with this, it was also decided in the meeting that efforts to spread literacy in various regions of Pashtunkhwa will be intensified, because education is the most important necessity for building an informed nation. During the meeting, a number of leaders also presented reports regarding the problems of their regions and emphasized that achieving freedom is impossible without public unity.

In the end, the participants of the meeting pledged that they would sacrifice their lives for the freedom of Pashtunkhwa and would continue the struggle for the dignity of their homeland until the very end. The closing ceremony of the meeting was held with a prayer, and all participants returned to their regions with a new resolve.

1271.right: What was written in the last issue regarding the People's Revolution was a harbinger of such a dangerous outcome for all of us, which clearly and plainly shows us that if we become victims of the discord and ill intentions of others, the result for us will be nothing but destruction and ruin. On the other hand, it is also necessary to mention regarding this subject that there are certain causes for the emergence of this revolution that had been hidden among the people for a long time. It is understandable for everyone that when a government turns a blind eye to the rights of its people and uses the path of oppression and force against them, then with the arrival of that time, the signs of the decline and fall of that government also appear. It is also important that if a government does not take any concrete steps for the welfare and peace of its people, then the path is paved for the emergence of hatred and dissatisfaction among the people, and this in itself is a sign of the weakness and failure of that government, which paves the way for the end of its power.
1271.left: Choosing a policy for the nation that becomes a cause for the people's prosperity and progress is very essential for every government. If a government does not strive to protect the rights of its people, there is a possibility of a reaction emerging among the people that paves the way for social chaos and disorder. Therefore, it is necessary for every ruler to have full knowledge of their people's hopes and demands and to take steps for them that lead to the creation of public trust and their well-being. In conclusion, it must be said that establishing a just system for the happiness of the people and the protection of their rights is a priority for every government, and this is very important for their continuity and survival.

1272.right:
Peshawar: 12 August 1920 AD

Editorial Note

International Trade

Trade is a major factor in improving mutual relations among the people of the world and in helping one another for mutual benefit. If the people of one country hinder the interests of the people of other countries for their own gain, they are in reality creating a major obstacle in the path of the world's progress and prosperity. All the people of the world are like one family; if an individual helps another, it is a human and moral act, but if someone goes against the interests of another for their own gain, it is an act against humanity. Our dear country, Afghanistan, due to its geographical location, is situated in a place where it can become a major trade hub between Central Asia and India. However, our traders must understand that in the field of trade, they must observe the principles of honesty and mutual assistance, because the essence of trade is to fulfill the needs of the people, not just to make a profit.

Recently, reports have been received of improper actions by some people in the field of trade in certain areas, which is a matter of shame for all Afghans. We must understand that our country's economy is linked to trade, and if traders are not honest, the country's reputation is tarnished. It is the responsibility of every Afghan to use honesty in their dealings and strive for the progress of their country.

1292.right:
An article about public life

In these days when the lifestyles of many people in the world are changing, and world conditions are changing so rapidly that the inhabitants of many countries are making many changes in their past customs, it is necessary that we also think about the life of our nation. Unfortunately, there are some bad customs in our society that are not only obstacles to progress in our lives, but also cause the loss of our material and spiritual wealth. We must realize that any custom that does not align with Islamic rulings and the demands of the time should be reconsidered. For example, unnecessary expenses in wedding ceremonies, and actions during times of death and injury that are neither permissible from a religious perspective nor acceptable from a rational perspective, cause many families to be drowned in debt. The youth of our society, who are the pride of the future, must fight against such improper customs and organize their lives in the light of knowledge and wisdom. Likewise, the spirit of unity and brotherhood in society must be strengthened. We must not forget that the secret to the success of a nation lies only in unity and solidarity. If we want to live like other developed nations of the world, it is necessary to look for our past shortcomings and strive to correct them.
1292.left:
A few points regarding the pen and education

In the current era, the value of knowledge and wisdom is hidden from no one. Any nation that falls behind in the field of education will find the paths to progress closed to it. Regarding the power of the pen, it is said that it is greater than the power of the sword, because the pen can bring about a revolution in the thought and mind of a nation that cannot be achieved by swords. In our region, there are many obstacles in the way of promoting education, but we must understand that removing these obstacles is the duty of every one of us. It is also the responsibility of governments and academic societies to provide the environment for education. Fortunately, some efforts have recently begun to raise the level of people's knowledge. In our magazine, there have been many discussions on the importance of education, and it is hoped that our readers have been encouraged to move toward knowledge. Whenever a person learns to read and write, their way of viewing the world changes. They can distinguish between truth and falsehood. In conclusion, it must be said that the importance of education and the pen in the life of a nation is like the water of life; if this water dries up, the life of the nation will also perish. So let us use all our efforts in the path of knowledge and the pen and take steps for the progress of our country.

In the meeting of Takkar
Speech of Fakhr-e-Afghan Sahib

But dear sisters and sweet brothers! You are aware of why we have gathered here today. That is, this meeting is being held in memory of those brave youths of Takkar who shed their precious blood in the path of the freedom of Islam, the country, and the nation. You might think that this Takkar incident is something new. But this incident of Takkar is not a new game. Read the history of all free nations; you will see countless incidents of this kind in it. Wherever a nation has freed itself from slavery and preserved its honor and modesty, such brave youths have always been born in that nation who did not care for their wealth or their heads, and sacrificed themselves in the pursuit of freedom, and sought it in their own blood for the sake of the homeland and honor.

Remember that the plant of a nation's freedom is watered with blood. And when this plant grows, then the silence of those who sacrificed their heads rests under its shade and finds peace. You are aware that the Pashtun nation had been captive to a foreign nation for twenty-six years. But when the time came, the blood of honor surged in the youths of the homeland, and they sacrificed their heads. So today, what a difference has come in our necks and cannons. Fifty years ago, there was no question, and now questions are being asked everywhere. If you understand, then what difference has arisen between the Pashtun of fifty years ago and the Pashtun of today? Why has this arisen? In truth, there were great Khans and leaders before, and very capable people were present. There were great scholars and wise men. But no one had put the country in danger; if they participated, they did so against the poor.

1326.right:
August 1920

The Muslim League and the Poet

Allama Sheikh Muhammad Iqbal is a poet among Orientalists whose fame for excellence has transcended the borders of the subcontinent. If this matter is doubtful in anyone's view, then for the measure of the popularity and fame of his poetry, it is enough that the discussions held regarding his poems among the members of the Indian Society of Orientalists (Anjuman-e-Khawar Shanas), and the praises bestowed by the Viceroy of India and the Governor of Punjab, are proof of this fact. Iqbal is a poet in the court of Orientalists who has opened the doors of scholarly and literary discussions among the world's Orientalists regarding his poetry.

We take great pride in the fact that a poet like Iqbal has been recognized as a great poet of our Islamic Ummah, and in his poetry, there is a spirit of reviving Islamic greatness and glory that kindles the passion of Islamic honor and unity in the heart of every Muslim. If we reflect deeply on Iqbal's poetry, it becomes clear that it contains very profound and scholarly content regarding the causes of the decline of Muslims, which in itself is a sign of his insight and understanding of the Ummah's pain. According to Iqbal's poetry, there is a need for such a revolution in the lives of Muslims that would change their path of life in the light of Islamic principles and enable them to succeed in competition with other nations of the world. Through his poetry, Iqbal has made such an effort to awaken the Muslims that it will remain alive forever in the pages of history, and under the influence of his thoughts, future generations will be able to find the way to regain their past glory.
1326.left:
August 1920

The main reasons for the decline of Muslims can be examined in the light of Iqbal's poetry. According to Iqbal, the biggest reason for the decline of Muslims is their distance from knowledge and wisdom and the forgetting of their own Islamic traditions. In his view, when the taste for studying their past glory ends for a nation, the decline of that nation begins right there. In his poetry, Iqbal has provided such guidance regarding the unity of Muslims and the regaining of their moral and spiritual strength that it serves as a beacon for the Muslims of today. Iqbal says that for the progress of Muslims, a balance of knowledge of both religion and the world is necessary, and this balance brings such equilibrium in a person's personality that they can be successful in every field of life.

Through his poetry, Iqbal has dreamed of creating a new generation that stands on its own feet and, by holding its head high before other nations of the world, raises the flag of the greatness of Islamic civilization. Regarding his poetry, Iqbal says that his verse is not just a world of imagination, but a message for changing the world of reality that will serve as a guide for human life in every era.

(End)

Answer: Those people who are in the grip of such diseases that doctors are unable to treat, such as types of lung diseases for which doctors are hopeless of a cure, it is necessary to avoid sitting and socializing with such people. Because the effects of such a disease cause harm to the health of other people.

Oppression and Children

Answer: Yes, committing oppression against children has a major effect on the destruction of their character and habits. When a kind of carelessness and heartlessness is created in children due to the oppression of their parents, then in the future, those children have a very bad effect on the country and the nation. This is a part of their nature.

Question: Is it correct, and what is the ruling in Islam regarding shedding tears and expressing grief for someone after their death?

Answer: In Islam, being patient at the time of death and being content with the will of Allah Almighty is a part of faith. However, shedding tears and expressing heart-felt pain due to grief for someone is a demand of human nature, but one must not exceed Islamic limits in this.

Religion is a path to knowing God that every human needs in the course of their life. For this reason, there is a need for public awareness for unity in religion.

1361.right:
Pashtun Literary Memoir
25 December 1920 AD
Pashtun Literary Memoir at the Shrine of Khushal Khan Khattak
On August 28, 1920 AD, under the auspices of the Pashtun Literary Memoir, a grand poetry symposium and meeting was held near the shrine of Khushal Khan Khattak in memory of Khushal Khan Khattak in the history of Islam. This event is an example for the literary world and a new step for the development of Pashto literature. Many people came from the villages for this poetry symposium. Almost towards the base, with the increase of literary figures and writers, people had come for the success of this symposium. Khan Bahadur Agha Lal, from the Khan Sharif hill of Peshawar, performed the duties of president in connection with this symposium. At the beginning of the symposium, Maulana Abdul Qadir Sahib was given the opportunity to provide a detailed account of Khushal Khan Khattak's life, his literary services, and his importance to Pashto literature. In his view, Khushal Khan Khattak is a star of Pashto literature, a poet who holds a unique place in the hearts of the Pashtuns.
1361.left:
In the field of Pashtun literature, this poetry symposium is a great success for the Pashtun. At the end, thanks were given to all participants for the success of the symposium, and a promise was made to build a grand memorial in honor of Khushal Khan Khattak.

In the end, a collection of Khushal Khan Khattak's poems titled "Pashtun Adab" was published by the Pashtun Literary Tazkira organization, which is a gift for the lovers of Pashtun literature.

In this series, it appears that some people, in order to make their unreliable claims credible in the eyes of the people, put words and stories into people's mouths that have no connection to reason and logic. They assume that people will believe their vain and meaningless words as the truth. Such actions are, in reality, a sign of their ignorance and a disrespect to the dignity of humanity. We must protect ourselves from the words of such people and develop the ability to distinguish between truth and falsehood.

Furthermore, regarding the activities of these individuals, it must be said that they not only harm the intellectual health of society but also sow the seeds of distrust and division among the people. Society must be vigilant against such people and not allow their devilish and deceptive actions to take root in people's minds. Knowledge and honesty are the weapons that protect society against such individuals. To prevent such actions, great attention must be paid to the promotion of science and knowledge so that people have no doubt or ambiguity in understanding right from wrong.
1369.left: To prevent these actions, efforts must be made to raise the intellectual level of the people. Only in this way can we build a shield to defend our society against lies and deception. The light of knowledge and wisdom is necessary to eliminate these darknesses. Every individual has a responsibility to take steps in defense of the truth and not remain silent in the face of falsehood. It is the duty of every citizen to strive to speak the truth and seek the truth. Although the path of truth may be difficult, it leads to lasting success. In the end, it must be said that speaking the truth is a great virtue of humanity and plays a fundamental role in the progress of society.

1403.right:
Eid, and I will not even buy new clothes for this Eid.

Tamim Mian Sahib, Rasul Sahib, A.N.A. stood up on their feet.

On the eve of Eid al-Adha, I went to Shah Pashtun Khan's house to go to "Niamat Abad" village. He was sitting in a very beautiful room of his house, and with great enthusiasm, he wished me a happy Eid. In his conversation, he expressed great joy about Eid, saying: For me, Eid means the beginning of a new life. After this, there was a lot of discussion with Shah Pashtun Khan about the historical value of Eid and the culture and traditions of Pashtun society. He mentioned his efforts for the development of Pashto literature. In the end, with great sincerity, along with Eid prayers, he also prayed for the unity of the nation.
1403.left: In the end, many things were discussed with Shah Pashtun Khan regarding Eid, and he told me about his life experiences: that with the arrival of Eid, all the worries of my mind disappear and I prepare for a new beginning. The Eid celebration ceremonies with Shah Pashtun Khan's family and friends were very interesting. In the end, I thanked him for his hospitality, and by wishing him a happy Eid, I took my leave from "Nemat Abad" and came to my home. On this way, the moonlight of the Eid night and the silence of the environment became a cause for peace of heart. Eids are a great opportunity in a person's life for new hopes and for strengthening brotherhood.

1404.right:
Peshawar Diary
Prior to this, the event around that time was that on February 18th, a congratulatory telegram was received from the Viceroy of India in Kabul for the Amir of Kabul on the occasion of Eid. And the Foreign Minister of Kabul also sent a congratulatory telegram in response to this telegram in the name of the Viceroy of India. Similarly, the Foreign Minister of Kabul also sent a telegram to the Foreign Secretary of India regarding the appointment of an Indian ambassador in Kabul. The Kabul government expressed great happiness at this action of the Indian government and thanked the Indian government for it. From the exchange of these telegrams, it appears that the relations between the governments of Kabul and India have improved significantly compared to the past, and both sides are making great efforts to improve their mutual relations. It was also said that the Kabul government has decided to send a delegation to hold talks regarding the issues of both governments. The Kabul government will give some special instructions to this delegation, on which both countries will reach an agreement. From this news, it appears that a new era is about to begin regarding trade and other matters between Afghanistan and India.
1404.left: Regarding which individuals the Kabul government will form a delegation from, no official news has been released yet, but it is speculated that this delegation will consist of high-ranking government officials. The dispatching of this delegation suggests that the Kabul government wants to further strengthen its relations with the Indian government. Alongside this, news has also reached from Kabul that reforms have been initiated there based on a new model for education and other social affairs, for which a series of invitations to foreign countries has also begun. The Kabul government appears very optimistic about this series of reforms and is dreaming of a better future for its people.

Akhtar Shah realized that he had no other way to be released, so he decided to cooperate fully with the police in order to save himself from severe punishment. He began to talk about all the secret stories he had previously kept hidden, and in this way, he helped the police to arrest the other members of the group.
1405.left: Thus, with Akhtar Shah's confession, a group of thieves in the area fell into the clutches of the police. The police officer was very happy with Akhtar Shah's confession and immediately ordered the arrest of the other members of the group. With Akhtar Shah's help, the police were able to raid the thieves' hideout, arrest many of their members, and also recover the stolen goods. After this incident, the people of the area were very happy with this success of the police and praised the bravery and expertise of the police officer. Akhtar Shah, realizing that there was no way left for him to escape, confessed to his mistakes and surrendered himself to the clutches of the law.

1407.right:
On the teacher

In the first publication
Because the teacher had a series of students, something was written about the art teacher in the art school. In this, to fulfill the main purpose of this article and to understand the teacher's art and morals, a series of materials have been written. Another student has written a few sentences specifically about the teacher, which are very important materials for understanding his art and morals, and this is also an important step for understanding his art; therefore, we have included this material here in this publication.

A teacher is a king, but for what? While this teacher has a series of principles for the world of art due to having students, these principles themselves are a great reason for kingship, because a teacher rules like a king in the hearts of students due to his art. Although this rule is not by means of money, it is by means of knowledge and art.

These principles, which a teacher must himself understand, are that a student should act upon his advice and understand his words, and in the end, become a knowledgeable and artistic person like him.
1407.left:
Another student has written this about the teacher in this regard:

The teacher is a good example for kings. Thank God that there is no thought of kingship among our students. But it seems that this king is not a teacher of performance, and it is not an easy distinction. If a person rules because of a special art, there is no doubt that he will be a good teacher; rather, he will be a teacher who plays the role of a guide for every student. Like kingship, in art and other branches of life, a teacher is a great teacher for his student because of his skill in his art, and it is a proven fact that in the world of art, a teacher is a great king for his art, and there is no doubt that he is a good example for every student of his art.

The teacher himself knows that a student should act upon the teacher's advice in life. Another point worth mentioning is that in art, a teacher is not only a person who teaches art to a student, but he is also a person who acts as a good example for his student in terms of morals, and there is no doubt that an art teacher is a person for his student who guides him in all matters of his life and directs his efforts for the progress of his life, and in the end, because of his art, becomes the cause of his student's honor in the whole world.

But he could not make me understand this matter. Finally, when he got tired, he gestured to me to give him a pen and paper, so that I could write what I wanted to say to him. After a while, he brought a slate and pencil, and on it, I only wrote the word "newspaper" in English, and he took it. And with a gesture, I told him to take it to the office. The officer denied it. He took it—but until the evening prayer, I came back to the room, and with him, I had tea in the room. "To be continued"

(Abdul Ghaffar)

And he was twenty years old - but it is a blessing that he became a Muslim better than his own people - now that work will be done - when the people are satisfied. (And their affairs are decided by consultation among themselves) Whether the panchayat is good or bad - there is no point in arguing about it - I am just expressing Munshi Premchand's thoughts on the panchayat to the Pashtun readers.

The memories of Mirza Sahib and Malik Kaka are many - and the time when they were studying with Mirza Sahib's father - they were full of greed. Malik Kaka used to serve Mirza Sahib's father - he had done many favors for him - he had many things on his tongue and many things on his lips - and many spices were what he used to bring - and God knows if one thing was not in Malik Kaka's fate or if Mirza Sahib's father could not pay much attention - because Mirza Sahib's servant had grown up in the village and was not very literate - and Malik Kaka had not learned even the alphabet - they were very simple-hearted people - and Malik Kaka's pride was in his own words and deeds - and if it were Malik Kaka's pride - he would have been upset with Mirza Sahib - he was remembered by everyone - everyone would have bowed their heads to him - they used to respect him.

Mirza Sahib also grew up in the village - our such customs - the barber and the letter writer would write letters that no one else could read after them.

Mirza Sahib had an old aunt - who had ten acres of land - except for this poor woman, there was no one to take care of her - and she had been living at Mirza Sahib's house for a long time - Mirza Sahib.

A statement on the just and the unjust

"Mezzani" was born around the year 1804 in a village in the "Geneva" province in the land of the Afghans; his father was a poor physician and his mother was an intelligent midwife. For him, in the village, "Mezzani" was very weak, and from childhood, he had a love for the poor. When he became a young man, like others, he developed a love for serving the common people and took an interest in studying literature in university departments. It is a large part of this story that when he grew up, his family members saw him begin to speak out for the rights of the poor in the village; in the beginning, he spoke to the village elders on behalf of the poor. According to him, the poor are also entitled to the rights of this homeland, and work must be done to provide them with the facilities of life. However, this kind of help for the poor appeared very bad to the Khans and leaders of that time; they made many efforts to prevent this work of his, but Mezzani was firm in his resolve. Once, to help a beggar, he gave him bread and clothes from his own money; when people saw this, they were very surprised by this act of his. This was a stage in his life that showed people that the poor and the rich are equal before God; because of the effect of this, a new consciousness and knowledge began to emerge in his village.

1457.right:
Pashtun rule in India

Two hundred years ago, when new ideas emerged in the hearts of Pashtuns regarding the decline of Pashtun rule in India, and much was said about the fall of the Pashtuns in India, this was the era of the Mughal Emperor Jalaluddin Akbar, who was very powerful in India. At that time, the talk in people's hearts regarding the Pashtuns of India was that the Mughal Emperor Akbar was trying to be hostile toward the Pashtuns and eliminate them. When the Pashtuns stood against Akbar Shah's government, the Pashtuns of India faced very great difficulties. Akbar Shah moved toward India with his army to crush the Pashtuns and subjected them to severe hardships. During the time when Akbar Shah was waging wars against the Pashtuns of India, the Pashtuns also stood against their enemy with great determination to defend their homeland. At that time, Akbar Shah had made major plans with his army to eliminate the Pashtuns. When the Pashtuns confronted Akbar Shah's army, they put up very strong resistance against it. In this war, the Pashtuns suffered great losses and were unable to continue opposing Akbar Shah's army. At this time, due to discord and lack of unity among the Pashtuns of India, Akbar Shah succeeded against them and paved his way to end the Pashtun rule in India. At this time, under a major plan to capture Pashtun territories, Akbar Shah sent his army to the Pashtun regions and subjected the Pashtuns to great suffering in their own lands. During this time, the Pashtun leaders became engaged in wars with Akbar Shah's army to protect their homeland, and by capturing the Pashtun territories, Akbar Shah further strengthened the foundations of his rule on Indian soil.
1457.left: During this time, the Pashtuns were subjected to many acts of oppression and tyranny by Akbar Shah's army, and since the Pashtuns were not united during that era, Akbar Shah took advantage of this opportunity to further increase his control over them; the difficulties that the Pashtuns faced during this period have been recorded as a historical fact, and the circumstances of that time had a significant impact on many aspects of Pashtun life, leaving deep effects on the foundations of their political and economic life.

1459.right:
Pashtun Heroes -- 49 -- 21 September 1920
My heart trembles with the pride of Afghan identity, because in the fold of this pride lies the expression of that existence and the symbol of the honor and dignity of that nation, which has left such echoes of glory in the world that even today every honorable Afghan takes pride in them. There is no room for doubt that in the field of honor and courage, that wave of the bravery of Ahmad Shah Baba's army, which was dancing towards India as a powerful army of the Islamic world, and left this mark in the fear of its enemies' hearts, that this is a courageous nation that confronts all kinds of invaders at the cost of their lives. But if we turn the pages of history in search of such past waves, our eyes rest upon a hero like Ubaidullah Khan and the self-sacrifice and devotion of Ahmad Shah Baba's army, who did not care for their lives or wealth in this path of honor. Throughout his life, he created such epics for the freedom of the homeland that will be written in golden letters on the pages of history forever. The stories of this hero's courage and bravery still teach every young person a lesson in defending the country today. He left behind such examples in his actions that they served as an unbreakable force against all forms of colonialism and tyranny. (Maulana Najibullah)
1459.left:
Pashtun Hero
As previously mentioned, this story of Ubaidullah Khan's courage and bravery is not only a lesson for the country's freedom, but an important chapter of that struggle which was launched for the pride of the Pashtun nation. Considering the circumstances of that day, it becomes clear that the courage of Ubaidullah Khan and the sacrifices of his companions actually raised a great storm of fear in the heart of the British colonialism of that time. From these pages of history, it is also evident that it was impossible for any kind of forces to stand against the honor and bravery of the Pashtuns. The struggle of these heroes was not only for the protection of a land, but for the protection of that pride and dignity which has been inherited by the Pashtun nation from history for centuries.

Afghanistan Independence Day
On May 28, 1939, the twenty-first Independence Day of the Pashtun nation
was completed with splendor, majesty, and happiness. On this
occasion in Peshawar, Mr. Muhammad Hakim Khan, a lawyer, invited the Pashtuns
and hosted a grand feast in honor of the respected Pashtuns. And on the
occasion of the feast, the honorable Muhammad Hakim Khan, to the respected guests
spoke in praise of Pashto. In it, he mentioned the famous name
of Ghazi Muhammad Nadir Khan, the conqueror, and described his eternal achievements. And the current
blessings of the government of His Majesty King Muhammad Zahir Shah
he explained - and along with it, the highness of Sardar Muhammad Hashim Khan
and His Highness Sardar Shah Wali Khan and His Highness Sardar Shah
Mahmud Khan's great achievements were praised - and the ceremony
ended with great happiness.
We, from the east, congratulate the Pashtun nation on this glorious day
and salute the spirit of the freedom-loving Pashtun nation.

A look at Albania

Albania's (late) King "Ahmed Zogu" is one of those figures who rose above the ordinary status of his merit and courage.

The story of the death of this king's father, Jalal Beg, is among the tribes of Albania. Besides the status of his own business, Jalal Beg was the trusted deputy of Sultan Abdul Hamid. He was born in 1895. Ahmed Zogu was raised in Albania in a way that prepared him for the path of leadership. Until 1915, Albania was part of the Turkish government. But when a freedom movement started against the Sultan's faulty government in Turkey, the idea of liberating his homeland began in Ahmed Zogu's heart. At the age of twenty, he joined the movement. He endured exile, imprisonment, and the hardships of war. Finally, he succeeded in his goal. In 1925, he became the Prime Minister of Albania, and in 1925, he became the head of Albania. Finally, in 1928, due to his ability and power, he was made King of Albania and took the title "Zogu".

During the time of the freedom movement, he faced many enemies. The people of Albania, like the Wazirs, believed in blood feuds. Controlling these bloodthirsty people was not an easy task. Ahmed Zogu was a brave man. He succeeded in controlling them. He was a target for his enemies. There were reports of him being targeted for assassination over three hundred (300) times. Many attempts were made on his life, but fate saved him, and he remained alive.

He kept his palace under the protection of machine guns and often did not participate in public meetings.

Ahmed Zogu was a very learned man. He could speak German, French, Turkish, and Serbian. He was fond of studying history and spent his lonely nights busy with work for the betterment of the country.

Zogu was very skilled in maintaining law and order among the people. He brought them under control through his behavior with his subjects. Whenever he heard that someone intended to rebel, he would call them to the palace and bring them under control through his way of dealing with them.

A priest, Fan Noli, was his very staunch enemy. When Zogu came to power, he exiled him. He was living in America. Finally, he became very ill, and the money for his treatment ---

A message of condolence from Pashtun
The struggle of Khan Sahib Khudai Dad Khan for the service of the nation is an example that will always be a torch for future generations. He spent a large part of his life for the unity of the Pashtuns and for winning their rights. In his death, not only his family but the entire Pashtun nation is in grief. Remembering his services and following his path is the duty of every Pashtun. We pray for his forgiveness in the court of God. May Allah Almighty grant patience to his family and all his friends. Amen.

1510.right:
Pashtun Utmanzai
21 June 1939
A message of condolence from Pashtun on the grief of the passing of Khan Sahib Khudai Dad Khan
Alas and a hundred times alas that a great leader like Khan Sahib Khudai Dad Khan, a fighter for the freedom of the homeland who always raised his voice against the oppression and tyranny of the British, and who understood the pain and sorrow of the nation's heart, is no longer among us today. His passing is a great tragedy for the entire nation. In this grief, not only his family and friends, but all those who dreamed of the independence and prosperity of the homeland are in mourning. The history of Khan Sahib Khudai Dad Khan's life and struggle is a shining example for those who are prepared to sacrifice their lives for the path of truth and reality. With his death, a page of the struggles of Pashtunkhwa has been turned. May God have mercy on him and grant him a place in Paradise. We express our sympathy to his family and survivors in this grief.

1682.right:
Tipu Sultan's Memory

30
August 1939 AD

In such a situation, when dark clouds of slavery were spread over many parts of India, in such a corner of the land of India, which is known as Mysore, a shining star emerged that lit the lamp of hope for freedom in the hearts of Indians. This shining star was "Tipu Sultan", who dedicated his entire life to the path of freedom.

Tipu Sultan was not only a shrewd politician but also a brave military leader. He understood that for the freedom of India, a systematic and united voice was needed against the British. He established contacts with leaders from different parts of India and urged them to stand against colonialism.

An important part of his life was his confrontation with the British. He defeated the British armies in many battles and prevented their expansionist policies. His bravery and perseverance were a source of inspiration for the people of that time.

But unfortunately, due to some traitors and allies of foreigners, Tipu Sultan joined the ranks of martyrs in an important battle. His death was a great loss in India's struggle for freedom, but his message and love for freedom remained forever in the hearts of Indians.

In conclusion, we can say that Tipu Sultan's struggle is an excellent example of an untiring effort for justice. He believed that freedom is the right of every human being and that any sacrifice for this right is permissible. Although he is not among us today, his achievements and his love for the homeland are forever written in our history.

It is essential for us to learn this lesson from Tipu Sultan's life: to always have the spirit of sacrifice for the freedom and dignity of our homeland. If we want to leave a dignified and free India for our future generations, then we must follow in the footsteps of leaders who sacrificed their lives for truth and justice.

This lamp of freedom that Tipu Sultan lit, today we all must collectively preserve. It is our national duty to keep the memory of such heroes fresh and to work for the progress of our country according to their guidance. Tipu Sultan's soul will be happy when we stand on our own feet for the freedom and survival of our homeland.

1755.right:
Pashtun Editorial
This monthly magazine named "Pashtun," published in 1929, discusses on this page the importance of unity, brotherhood, and mutual assistance among Pashtuns. At the beginning of the text, a call for Pashtun unity is made, followed by a detailed explanation of its benefits and the harms of discord. The text begins as follows:
The benefit of the nation is the benefit of every Pashtun; therefore, it is necessary for all to unite. For the progress of this nation, the path of consensus should be taken instead of prejudice. If we unite among ourselves, no one will dare to look at us with ill intent. This article also emphasizes the importance of knowledge and education, and calls upon the youth to strive for education in order to serve their nation. The article concludes with a slogan for the unity of the Pashtun nation.
1755.left: In my opinion, if we want to become a strong nation, we must adapt ourselves to the demands of the times while preserving our traditions. In particular, women's education and the training of the youth are what shape our future. In every section of this issue of Pashtun, various stories and advice regarding unity have been written. This magazine presents a vivid picture of the social situation of that time and is a step towards efforts for unity among the Pashtuns. It is hoped that the contents of this magazine will bring about a positive change in the minds of the readers.

War Preparations in Iran and Iraq The Egyptian newspaper writes that war preparations are underway in Iran. There are reports of a large army gathering in Qazvin, Khorasan, and Isfahan. There are reports of army concentration in the western parts of Iraq, towards the desert of Western Iraq, along the border of Iran. In this regard, there are also reports of some other military activities in the eastern and northern parts of Iran. This is a cause for great concern. Because as a result of these actions, a kind of crisis can arise in the relations between Iran and these countries.
A new series of talks between Iran and Iraq regarding the border and walls is also a cause for concern. No new news has been released by the Iraqi government in this regard. However, there are indications of specific measures being taken by Iran in response to these actions. The possibility of continued conflict over the borders between the two countries is high, and regional stability is threatened.

Page 30

11 November 1931

The decision of the Grand National Jirga

And the reasons for taking practical steps

A petition

We have received news that in various places, rumors are circulating that a group of people has published a document among themselves that is having a very negative impact on the people, and such talk spreads disunity within the nation. Regarding this document, we clarify the following:

(1) Sayyid Abdul Rahman Sahib Kakhel is a person whose words and actions have always been driven by the spirit of goodwill for the nation, and he has always strived for the unity and harmony of the nation; the accusations published against him are baseless.

(2) Mian Attaullah Sahib Kakhel is a person who has always played his intellectual and practical part for the progress of his nation, and the accusations published against him are far from the truth.

(3) With the publication of Karamat Shah Sahib's letter of appreciation (Spasnama) of Polad, it became clear that his intention and that of his companions is for the unity of the nation, and he has always remained steadfast on the path of sacrifice for the freedom of the country.

(4) Regarding the aforementioned Khan and the document mentioned above, much more is being said, but by looking at his past life and achievements, it is proven that he has always strived for the pride of his nation and stands firm against all kinds of conspiracies.
1789.left:
In this regard, we firmly state that such rumors are spread to create discord among the people and to work for the interests of the colonialists. We call upon all patriots and nationalists not to be deceived by such conspiracies.

It has been decided by the members of the Grand Tribal Council that the entire nation will remain united and will work together to achieve independence. We stand against anyone who creates obstacles to the unity of the nation.

Spread this decision in all regions so that all people become aware of the truth. We must maintain an atmosphere of brotherhood among ourselves and not fall into the conspiracies of outsiders.

We are firm in our goal and will not refrain from any sacrifice to achieve independence. The path to freedom is difficult, but with the unity of the nation, this path will become easy.

Announcement of the Salar-e-Azam (Supreme Commander)

I, in the capacity of Salar-e-Azam, convey the message of their people to all the public, that they are in a delicate time, and before the command of God Almighty, I am in Peshawar at such a time, whether in this or that time, the financial distress of the fighters has been prevented, and they have been engaged in extraordinary controversial or deceptive programs—and if they are sitting, then for the sake of relocating them and coordinating with them, in such a delicate time of war, there is a dire need for workers and experienced people by the grace of God Almighty.

I appeal to my soldiers for the sake of God—and I appeal for their service—where you have dedicated yourself and your life to your brothers in the war of freedom—today again, offer your services for your dear nation.

There is no doubt that in the last two or three years, the complaints of the brothers of the Khudai Khidmatgars have reached from various places—and they have placed the burden on their own conscience—but for the sake of the nation's interest, they have not asked for anything—and in such a time, they are forgotten—and they are in support of their national brothers—and have done a favor to their nation on another foundation—and proved to the world that the Pashtun nation has always been ahead of other nations of the world in achieving freedom. Pashto Orthography 2



Question: What is the name of the letter (ځ), what is its shape, and what is its sound?
Answer: The name of the letter (ځ) is "Dzay", and this letter is written in words in the Pashto orthography in the following way, such as:
Dzān (self), Dzay (go), Dzam (I go), Dzaghawul (to run), Dzal (shine), Dzangal (forest), Dzay (place), Dzo (we go), Dzi (he/she goes), Dzaka (because), Dzawab (answer), Dzangary (special), Dzo-dzi (offspring), Dzoredal (to suffer), Dziyag (rough), Dzand (delay), Dzankadan (death throes), Dzangary (special).

Question: In which places does the letter (ځ) appear?
Answer: The letter (ځ) is used in many places in words in the Pashto language, such as at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, but in Pashto orthography, this letter also appears in many places instead of (ز), for the understanding of which one must act according to the rules and principles of the Pashto language.
1855.left:
The use of the letter (ځ) in Pashto orthography is very important in the pronunciation of words, because in many words the difference between (ځ) and (ز) changes the meaning of the word, such as (ځان) and (زان), which both have distinct meanings in Pashto.

In the same way, the principles of using other letters in Pashto are also understandable in this manner. For reading and writing the Pashto language, it is necessary that the shapes and sounds of the letters are correctly identified.

At the end of this section, we can say that the use of the letter (ځ) is one of the fundamental letters in standard Pashto orthography, which helps in the sweetness and correct pronunciation of the language. For the growth and development of the Pashto language, such precise rules must be followed.

This action is a very useful and commendable step for the growth and nurturing of the Pashto language, which is considered a great victory for the empowerment of the Pashto language against the propaganda of the country's enemies. The duty of this academy will be to collect the sciences, literature, and ancient works of Pashto, and to conduct scientific research.

Recently, the government of Afghanistan has paid special attention to the establishment of a scientific and literary academy for the Pashto language, which is considered the beginning of a new era.

For today's youth, it is very important to combine religious and worldly knowledge in their studies, so that in the future they may lay the foundation of a true and happy society. It is our endeavor that the love of the homeland and the service of religion be planted in everyone's heart in such a way that it becomes stronger with the passage of time. It is every person's right to have their own opinion, but this opinion must emerge from a path that leads to the benefit and well-being of all. In this way, our homeland will be saved from all kinds of problems and will take steps on the path of progress and prosperity. It is the duty of faith and conscience of every Afghan to stop at nothing in the service of their homeland and their nation. Every step taken on this path of life should be a bearer of a new light and a new hope.

Greek Philosophy and Us

Imitating others and following the customs and traditions of ancestors is the work of common people. A scholar is required not to imitate anyone else, but rather to weigh every matter on the scale of his own intellect; if it is correct, he should act upon it, and if it is wrong, he should cast it into the pit.

It is a pity that today we do not act upon this principle. We never ponder over the fact that what is the benefit of the logic and philosophy that we study day and night. Does this serve religion? Or does it protect the homeland? We have read books ourselves over time. Now we show them to other people, and we do not look at all at whether these sciences provide any benefit, or if our precious time is just being wasted on them.

The true purpose of logic and philosophy - the purpose of logic was to learn how to speak. But the amount of logic that is being taught as a foundation - from which one can neither make useful remarks according to the occasion in a gathering, nor deliver an eloquent speech on an issue. So what is the point of this?

The purpose of philosophy was this - that philosophy attempts to reach the roots and foundations of everything, but the number of philosophers who look at a book without understanding its essence, they never even imagine that it could be shown in the glass of something. So they write it down.

1945.right:
Education in the past (6)

For the Pashtun and the people of Pashtunkhwa, for those people who are in a stupor and do not know what the state of other nations of the world is, we are publishing this article in the Pashto language as follows:

Question: Are the people of Pashtunkhwa aware of the state of other nations or not?
Answer: Very little, because many people of Pashtunkhwa are deprived of education and do not understand how the world's conditions are changing.

Question: Is education necessary for the progress of Pashtunkhwa?
Answer: Absolutely, education is recognized as an essential step for the progress of every nation.

Question: What kind of efforts are needed for the education of the people of Pashtunkhwa?
Answer: First and foremost, there is a need to build schools and reform madrasas, so that people become familiar with modern sciences.

Question: Do the people of Pashtunkhwa recognize the obstacles in the path of their own well-being?
Answer: Yes, but unfortunately, due to ignorance, they often follow the wrong paths.
1945.left:
Question: What is the role of newspapers and media in awakening the people of Pashtunkhwa?
Answer: Media can play a very important role if broadcasts are made in their language and culture.

Question: Do the people of Pashtunkhwa love their language and literature?
Answer: Yes, the people of Pashtunkhwa have a deep love for their language and literature, but due to a lack of education, they cannot preserve it properly.

Question: What is the responsibility of the people of Pashtunkhwa for the future generation?
Answer: The greatest responsibility is their education and upbringing, so that they can stand on their own feet for their future.

Question: In the end, what is your message for the people of Pashtunkhwa?
Answer: The people of Pashtunkhwa must adopt the path of knowledge and step onto the path of unity and brotherhood, because without unity, their success is impossible.

1994.right: In the first place, regarding the type of government structures, the Montagu-Chelmsford report indicates that in the process of forming a Federation for India, it is proposed to introduce a series of changes in the central part—beyond the way current governments operate—based on a new model for a federal government policy. This proposal suggests that representatives of India's various provinces will work together for the interests of all of India in coordination with the central government within the framework of a federal council. In the course of this proposal, it is also considered that in the future, a law should be enacted regarding the distribution of powers between provincial autonomy and the central government, so that based on it, the path is paved for increasing the participation of the people of India in the structure of the federal government.
1994.left: Along with this, a series of recommendations have also been made in this report for the rights of minorities and their protection. In addition to this, it has also been considered that the participation of the people in the administration of civil affairs should be increased and a series of public consultations regarding government policies for solving their problems should be initiated. 1998.right: In the series of my initial writings regarding the situation of Muslims in India, I have repeatedly discussed the political and social state of Muslims in this country, and there is no doubt that the current state of India's Muslims, especially in the field of their education and religious studies, is a cause for concern. Although I acknowledge that the efforts of some leaders in this country regarding the unity of Muslims are commendable, there are still many signs of discord among their political activities. While a number of Muslim leaders are making efforts to join certain political groups or to cooperate closely with the Indian National Congress, on the other hand, there is another side that firmly insists on a separate political status for Muslims and the protection of religious values. These contradictions have caused deep fragmentation and discord to emerge among Muslims. In my opinion, if Muslims want to maintain their position in Indian politics, it is necessary to take steps toward uniting their scattered ranks and to create a common path while keeping their religious and national interests in mind.

2067.right:
Pashtun Utmanzai 17 May 1928

A piece of good news
In accordance with the decision of the provincial council of Fakhr-e-Afghan Inayatullah Khan, Fakhr-e-Afghan Sahib, along with Arbab Abdul Ghafoor Khan, delivered speeches on April 28 in Bannu and other places, including Dera Ismail Khan and Kohat districts, regarding the preaching of Khudai Khidmatgars and preparations for future struggle. They brought the conditions for Arbab Sahib's stay and requested a national Jirga. On April 20, the Pashtun Tanu camp and conference were held on April 26, 27, and 28 in the Tanu circle, where a magnificent camp and a grand conference of the Khudai Khidmatgars of the area took place. The conference was presided over by Qazi Ataullah Khan Sahib. The Minister of Education and Pashtun Fakhr-e-Afghan Sahib also participated and spoke at this conference, and in addition to them, thousands of national workers joined in.

Delhi Azad Muslim Conference: On the 27th and 28th, a grand conference of all-India liberal Muslim groups and others was held in Delhi. Khan Bahadur Allah Bakhsh, the Prime Minister of Sindh, presided over it and stated that this conference supported the Congress policy and opposed the Muslim League's Pakistan proposal.

Khaksar Civil Disobedience: After the tragic incident of March 31, Mr. Muhammad Ali Jinnah Sahib was holding peace talks with the Punjab government. However, it became known that there was no success in it; now the Khaksars are violating the law in Lahore and are being arrested.

Beware of the mosquito of malaria
O intoxicated ones! Do you protect yourselves from the malaria mosquito? It is a type of mosquito from whose larvae malaria fever originates. This mosquito sucks blood from the human body at the time of biting. Then the germs spread throughout the human blood and increase in number.
Here, after the monsoon, it usually starts in the wind. It remains in full force during the months of Asar and Katik, and this is the time when rice is planted in the fields. If this mosquito is the main cause of the fever, then at this time, it is necessary to protect oneself well from mosquito bites.
When three things come together, malaria fever originates from them. If any one of these three things is removed, then malaria fever will also disappear. Those things are as follows:
First, human beings. Second, mosquitoes. And third, malaria germs. It is necessary to protect human beings from the malaria mosquito. Why is it necessary to destroy the mosquito's larvae? Because if they are destroyed, people will be free from fevers. For their destruction, these few things are necessary.
(1) Protecting oneself from mosquito bites.
(2) Eradicating mosquitoes and their larvae.
(3) Informing people about the causes of malaria fever.
(4) Treating malaria fever completely with the medicines of the physicians.

2079.right:
(A) One should protect children from mosquitoes in such a way that sensible people do not build houses for themselves where thin iron mesh screens are not installed on their doors and windows, so that mosquitoes cannot enter through them.
(B) If possible, build two-story rooms for sleeping and sleep on the upper floor, because mosquitoes cannot fly very high.
(C) Avoid having too many dark corners in the sleeping room, because mosquitoes hide in the shadows of dark corners during the day and come out from there at sunset.
(D) Village ponds should be located far away from houses on high ground, and if possible, trees that grow quickly should be planted around them, such as willow, poplar, or other similar trees; the benefit of this is that these trees dry up the water.
In the sleeping room, one should be careful about light, because mosquitoes hide from sunlight but are very fond of lamp light. If a light is turned on near the sleeping room, all the mosquitoes will gather there, and in this way, one can get rid of mosquitoes.

I want to make it clear to you that on the previous occasion, I agreed that we had started the civil disobedience movement, even though the conditions I had proposed had not been met. But on this occasion, I am very strict. I want you to understand that any general who leads a war must necessarily make his army understand the conditions for starting the war. Within our ranks, there will be more difficulties than before. These will be of two types: one external and one internal. Britain is in a war of violence.

In addition to the Persian and Arabic letters in the old Pashto alphabet, four letters have been adopted as Pashto's own, which are: 'ځ' (dz), its name is 'dzir' and it gives the sound of 'z'. 'څ' (ts), its name is 'tsim' and it gives the sound of 's'. 'ځ' (dz), its name is 'dzin' and it gives the sound of 'kh', but besides this, another letter is very necessary. 'ڃ' (j), its name is 'j', it gives the sound of 'j'. Its shape is not of the 'ڃ' type, rather it is a letter that in some dialects like Wazir, Ghilji, etc., gives the sound of 'ږ' (zh), and in Yusufzai or standard Pashto, it gives the sound of 'ڃ' (j). For example, in the language where it is used, 'ژرا' (zhra) is called 'جرا' (jra), 'ورېځ' (wrezh) is called 'ورېج' (wrej), 'ژاول' (zhawal) is called 'جاول' (jawal), 'ږه' (zhe) is called 'جه' (je), 'ږند' (zhind) is called 'جرنده' (jranda), 'ږوبل' (zhobal) is called 'جوبل' (jobal), 'ږدل' (zhdal) is called 'وجل' (wjal), 'ږوښت' (zhwesht) is called 'جوړه' (jora), 'ږوند' (zhwand) is called 'جوند' (jwand), and 'روښې' (rwashe) is called 'روجر' (rwajer). Until now, for these words, scribes generally use either 'ږ' or 'ج', while there is a need for another letter for this. In my opinion, if a 'ډ' (d) is placed on top, then this would be a new letter, which those in the east would read as 'ډ' and those in Pashtunkhwa or Yusufzai would read as 'ږ'. This would make it clear.
I hope that the Pashto scholars will consider this and give appropriate advice.
(Editorial)

Socialism and Islam

Nowadays, when socialism is mentioned in the world, it has five
principles - which are written below!
(1) The government's relationship is only with the common people, it is not
a monopoly of a specific person or a family.
(2) All citizens of the country are equal in every respect. There is no
distinction between them except for service.
(3) The government treasury is the property of the common people. Whoever
the common people appoint as their leader, he has the authority to serve the treasury.

to help meet the needs of every person lies with the government.
(5) No single thing can become anyone's private property.

11 May, year 1920 AD
Advertisement of the Waqf Board
Mian Jafar Shah Sahib, Secretary of the Waqf Board of the Frontier, has published an advertisement in the form of a warning. The content is as follows: The office of the Provincial Waqf Board has been established behind the Kabuli Gate in Peshawar, in the building of Mian Feroz Shah, son of Khayinan. Branches of this board have been established in all districts except Mardan (it will also start in Mardan very soon). Mutawallis (trustees) of Waqf—and those persons who have any connection with Auqaf—are informed that from 10 May 1920 AD until the end of this month, they should send their applications for registration to the Provincial Auqaf Office through their district committees. Printed application forms and maps can be obtained from the office for a price. Each form and map will be provided for two paisas. With every application, a duplicate copy of the map for the district committee office is also required. Whoever applies, should write two sets of applications for the provincial office—one for the office or the district committee office. The district committee, after verification, will send one application with its report to the provincial office and keep one with itself. With every application, an eight-anna fee will also be paid, for which a receipt will be given.

Committee formed
On April 22, in Haryan, the Malakand Agency National Jirga
session was held under the chairmanship of Khan Rahat Khan Sahib.
Maulana Fazal Mahmood Sahib, General Secretary, presented the Jirga's
proposal which was unanimously approved. Besides this, three
other proposals were also approved. And copies of these were sent to the Governor of the Frontier and
the Political Agent of Malakand.
(1) There is a very dire need for the spread of education in the Malakand Agency area.

least an Anglo-Vernacular Middle School is definitely necessary.
(3) The restriction that has been placed on the population in the Agency - this
should be lifted. This is causing great hardship to the poor people.

Latab Khan, Secretary of Malakand Agency, in Apekang

One might think that Pashto is very harsh in a literary sense, but if you ponder a little, there is no other language in the world like Pashto, whose words are as colorful and beautiful as those in Pashto. In it, there are words that, by changing their meaning, allow a single word to provide dozens of meanings. Now you judge for yourself how vast another language could be compared to Pashto. Lovers of the Pashto language should understand that Pashto is a language that, in every era and in every place, makes a full effort to preserve its vocabulary in its own sweet and charming way. If the Pashtuns understand the Pashto language and strive to comprehend it, then this language can very quickly compete with other languages of the world. Therefore, Pashtuns must take action for the progress of Pashto and record their honors, culture, and history in the Pashto language, so that the value of the Pashto language may be known in every corner of the world.
These lovers of the Pashto language should also keep in mind that the Pashto language is not only tied to the Pashtuns, but this language holds a special status throughout the world.
Therefore, striving for the progress of the Pashto language is the duty of every Pashtun.

2154.right: In 1920, the British Imperial delegation emphasized in the ministers' debate that India should be given a government that is in accordance with the vote of the people of India and is for the people of India, by the people of India, which meant that the British had acknowledged that India should be granted autonomy. For this purpose, a delegation was appointed according to the demand of the people of India, but regarding the members of this delegation, there was a very big reason for doubt and suspicion in the minds of the people of India about the intentions of the British, because this delegation was entirely formed by the employees of the British government and no representatives of the people of India were included in it. Furthermore, at the time of appointing this delegation, no consultation was held with the people of India; rather, this action was imposed on the people of India by force, and this was at a time when, according to the demand of the people of India, a free and independent government of the people should have been formed in India, and along with this, there was also the matter that the right to the government formed by the people of India as a free nation should belong to the people, and the decision regarding it should be in the hands of the people.
2154.left: In addition to this, in the series of demands, it cannot be denied that the leaders of the war of independence stated that the laws enforced in India by the British government, and on the basis of which British rule was continuing in India, should be replaced—in accordance with the demands of the people of India and the wishes of the leaders of the war of independence—by a new law, created according to the will of the people of India, that would pave a permanent path for the independence of the people of India.

May God accept this prayer of mine with sincerity and full devotion, that by the grace of God and the kindness of the village, for the welfare of the village, wherever they may be—whether in a madrasa, a school, or other religious places—may God protect all the people of this village from evil and mischief, and may God grant this village the ability for progress and welfare, and may the people of our village unite and cooperate with one another in the work of developing our village, so that through this, by the grace of God, progress may be bestowed upon our village, and may our village be safe from every kind of evil and mischief, and by the grace of God, may the light of knowledge and art be bestowed upon our village, and may the people of our village, by the grace of God, take steps on the path of knowledge and wisdom.
2217.left:
With full sincerity in this address, may God accept this prayer that our village remains safe from every kind of evil and harm, and that we become capable of every kind of work and service for the betterment of our village, and through this, by the grace of God, progress may be bestowed upon our village, and the people of our village may unite and agree with one another in the works of developing their village, so that through this, the light of knowledge and art may be bestowed upon our village.

(Written by Mr. Abdul Malik Khan Sahib)

2229.right:
Volume Four: Pashtun

Regarding the causes of the fall of the former government of Afghanistan: To tell the truth, the roots of Afghanistan's great revolution lie in the womb of misfortunes from long ago. This first spark of revolution and the price of the corruption of oppression, which was started by the country's hereditary government, is very regrettable. When the price of oppression in a country becomes high and people are tied to each other in shackles of cruelty and tyranny by government officials, then the price of the government's ignorance becomes the cause of great poverty among the people. Revolutions come when the distance between the government and the nation increases and people are tied to each other in circles of cruelty and tyranny due to the government's incorrect policies. Maulana Muhammad Ibrahim Sahib mentions in his discussions that among the reasons for the collapse of our country's government, in addition to the lack of science and knowledge, people had fallen into a pit of misery. Regarding this revolution, the government's incorrect measures and the ignorance of the rulers caused the nation to rise against the government. Along with this, the roots of internal conflicts and enmity in the country caused the reasons for the government's collapse to hinder the country's progress one after another. Regarding all these problems, one of the biggest causes of the misery of the people of Afghanistan is the lack of education and knowledge in the country.
2229.left:
In this context, if one looks at the politics of the government of that time and the life of the common people, it seems that the distance between the government and the nation was widening day by day. Due to the ignorance of government officials, bribery, and injustice, the people were drowned in a pool of hopelessness. Along with this, the weakness of the country's economic situation and the lack of any specific program for the welfare of the people were the points that paved the way for the collapse of the government. At that time, no steps had been taken for the development of educational and cultural activities, and the level of awareness of the country's people was at a very low level. As a result of all these factors, the causes of the country's decline created a sense of hatred and revenge in the hearts of the people. M.BASHIR
Private Secretary
Board of Education

News of 1 June 1920

Khan Abdul Qayyum Khan, Barrister, has reached an understanding with the honorable head of the Kabul Post Office, Ataullah Shah Sahib Mukhlis, in which they have promised me every kind of assistance in the Post and Telegraph Department. Although for a long time there had been a request from the Post and Telegraph Department that a special arrangement was needed for the exchange of mail with the Peshawar Post and Telegraph Department, unfortunately, due to the lethargy and negligence of the Kabul postal officials, these matters were hindered. Now, thank God, this understanding has been reached between these two sides. As a result of this understanding, there has been great ease in the transport of mail between Kabul and Peshawar, and the waiting time for people to receive mail will be reduced. With the implementation of this understanding, the communication system between both sides will be strengthened. (Editorial)

2243.right:
Eid and its result

Because this is the day of Eid and there is happiness in people's hearts, it is necessary to write something as a lesson regarding the circumstances of this day. Someone said that this is the day of Eid and there is happiness among the people, but in reality, this is a day of sorrow for him. Because everyone knows that this is the day of Eid, but on this day, the fire of grief is lit in everyone's heart, because with the arrival of Eid, the memory of his loved ones is refreshed and the sound of pain comes out of his mouth. On this day, instead of happiness, there is mourning in everyone's house, and there is a flood of tears in everyone's eyes. Someone said that on this day there is a fire of love in people's hearts, but in reality, this is a day of hatred and malice. Because on this day everyone is looking for enmity with each other, and is thinking of each other's evil. On this day, everyone is thinking of themselves and is unaware of the condition of others. Alas! People celebrate this Eid to fulfill their enmities with each other, not to find a way of brotherhood and love with each other. The king is also a king, but on this day there is mourning in the king's house too, because the number of the king's enemies is increasing day by day and the time for the decline of the king's rule is approaching. On this day, the king is thinking about protecting his throne and crown, and is trying to save himself from the evil of his enemies. On this day, there is an atmosphere of grief and anxiety in the king's court as well, and there are fears of the king's future evil in the hearts of the king's loyal servants.
2243.left:
Eid and its result (continuation)

On this day of Eid, many people gather in the king's court, but everyone has come for their own purpose. Because the king is also looking for new ways for himself on this day. On this day of Eid, everyone in the king's court is afraid of one another, because everyone knows that there is always a possibility of change in the king's court. On this day, there is a spirit of revenge against his enemies in the king's heart, and in his eyes are dreams of the destruction of his enemies. On this day, there is also fear of bad days in the hearts of the king's loyal ministers, because they know that the value of loyalty in the king's court has diminished. On this day, everyone is in search of power for themselves, and is trying to destroy others. In short, on this day of Eid, there is an atmosphere of sadness, enmity, and hopelessness everywhere. And this is the true result of Eid.

The king asked his courtiers in his court: "Is any one of you capable of identifying this treasure?" After the silence of many people, a brave young man came forward and said: "O King! I will use all my strength to find this secret." The king was pleased with his courage and allowed him to go in search of the treasure. Following the king's words, the young man set off towards the region where there were rumors about that treasure. He passed through difficult paths and dangerous places and finally reached the place where the signs of that treasure were. He investigated that area very carefully. After a few days passed, he found a hidden place which was the door to that treasure. He opened the door and saw the amazing sights of the treasure, which was full of gold and jewels. He returned to the king's court with great joy and gave the king full information about the location of the treasure. The king was very proud of his success and gave him many rewards for his services. The young man was now known as a hero in the country and attained a high position in the king's court. In the end, the king gave him full authority to manage the affairs of the treasure and he became a great servant for his country.
2244.left: This story about the secrets of the king's treasure is still very popular among people today and is considered a sign of his wisdom and courage. That young man not only gained his own wealth but also obtained a treasure of great value for his country. This story teaches us that if we are truthful and sincere in our goal, eventually the doors of success will open before us and we will be able to find the path to success in the difficult stages of life.
